Subject: MDM connector — what we can improve (config vs code)

Hi all,

Quick overview of what we can improve on the MDM connector, split into two groups: things we change in configuration (fast, no code release) and things that need code changes.

**Configuration changes — quick wins, no release needed**

- *Smaller work batches.* The connector currently takes on more work at once than it can finish in the time allowed, which forces it to restart the same batch repeatedly. Reducing the batch size fixes this. This is the main cause of the current backlog.
- *Use all available data streams.* The topic provides 8 parallel streams; the connector is currently set up to read only 2. Using all 8 gives us roughly four times the processing capacity.
- *Fixed capacity instead of auto-scaling.* Auto-scaling adds servers when CPU is high. This connector mostly waits on network responses, so CPU stays low and auto-scaling never triggers. Setting a fixed size is more predictable.
- *Faster failure detection.* If a request to MDM or Salesforce hangs, we currently wait 30 seconds. Reducing that lets the connector recover sooner.
- *A few missing settings* for provider records that are currently falling back to defaults pointing at a test environment.

**Code changes — need a release, more lasting benefit**

- *Remove an unnecessary lookup.* Every person record currently makes an extra call to Salesforce that was designed to be batched but was never switched on. Enabling it removes roughly one call per record.
- *Make the connector aware of its own deadline.* Today it accepts a batch of work with no sense of how long it has. Adding that awareness means it degrades gracefully instead of restarting from scratch.
- *Shut down cleanly.* When the connector restarts, in-progress work isn't allowed to finish first, so two versions can briefly overlap and duplicate effort.
- *Isolate individual failures.* One unexpected error currently stops all work in progress rather than just that record.
- *Prevent overlapping updates to the same person.* When two changes to the same person are processed at the same moment, one can silently overwrite the other.
- *Two record types have no handler* and currently fail after retrying. Wiring them up stops the noise.

**Separately — our deployment process**

We found that configuration changes have not been reaching the deployed connector: the deployment reports success before the change is actually applied. We're fixing this first, since none of the configuration changes above would take effect otherwise. This is likely why earlier tuning attempts appeared to have no impact.

**Suggested order**

1. Fix the deployment process
2. Apply the batch size change and confirm the backlog starts clearing
3. Increase to all 8 streams
4. Code changes in a following release

Steps 1 and 2 should resolve the immediate problem. The rest is about capacity and resilience.

Happy to go into more detail on any of these.

Thanks,
Adarsh
